1.sense: An instruction and then an answer. Someone had asked what this God is, expecting a description in the terms they already used for gods, and the reply refuses the terms rather than filling them in.

notes.t: Ahad is not the ordinary counting one, which is wahid. Wahid is one of a possible series; ahad is oneness that admits no second at all, which is why the word is almost never used of created things in the affirmative.
The occasion reported is that the idolaters, and in another narration a group of Jews, said: describe your Lord to us, and this was revealed. The narrations differ and their grading is discussed.
notes.src: Tirmidhi 3364 and others; the chains and gradings are disputed

notes.t: The surah begins with Say, which keeps it audibly a message being handed over rather than a statement the speaker thought of.

links.why: do not take two gods; He is only one God

2.sense: One word, and it is the hardest word in the surah to carry into English. Every translation of it is a choice among meanings the Arabic holds at once.

notes.t: The early generations gave several readings of as-Samad: the one every creature turns to in need and who needs nobody; the one who is solid all the way through, with no hollow, who does not eat or drink; the one complete in every attribute. These are not rival guesses so much as facets, and the exegetes preserved all of them.
notes.src: reports from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Hasan and others, collected by at-Tabari

notes.t: The verse repeats the name Allah instead of saying He, which in Arabic re-anchors the sentence and makes the second statement stand on its own rather than lean on the first.

links.why: you are the ones in need of Allah, and He is the Free of need

3.sense: Two denials, and between them they cut every family line a people has ever attached to a god: no offspring below, no origin above. Birth is how created things enter and continue, and He is outside it in both directions.

notes.t: The Qur'an makes the same denial elsewhere and argues it: how could He have a son when He has no companion, and He created all things.

The order matters. Did not beget comes first, answering the claims made in the Prophet's own city and beyond it; was not begotten follows, closing the question of where He came from before it can be asked.

links.why: the heavens almost rupture at the claim that the Most Merciful took a son

4.sense: The last door. Having denied Him a partner, a need and a lineage, the surah denies Him a peer of any kind, and closes on the same word it opened with.

notes.t: The Prophet ﷺ said of this surah that it is equal to a third of the Qur'an. The scholars explain the share as its subject rather than its reward: the Qur'an teaches creed, law and story, and this surah is creed in four verses.
Kufu is the word used for a marriage match, someone of comparable standing. Its use here denies not only rivalry but comparability.
Ahad opens verse one and closes verse four, so the surah is a ring. Whatever you were told in between, you are put back where you started.

links.why: there is nothing like unto Him
do you know of any namesake for Him
